relevance_note: Single case report of a boy with Blau syndrome and a genetically confirmed NOD2 mutation: "Genetic study confirmed an autosomal dominant mutation in the NOD2/CARD15 gene."
method_note: Built by a short Python script from my own reading of the paper; all spans checked verbatim by script. Two individuals: the patient (13-year-old boy) and his mother, who is in scope as an affected relative ('misdiagnosed as having rheumatoid arthritis as a child, after presenting similar symptoms'); the mother's 'similar symptoms' are not itemized, so she has no phenotypic_features rows and all checklist items are 'not reported'; she is not said to be genetically tested, so she has no variant row. The patient's NOD2 variant is not described (variant_original_string 'not reported'); 'autosomal dominant mutation' was not taken as a statement of zygosity or inheritance. Age at last evaluation uses the age at presentation ('13-year-old'); the last follow-up was 3 months after onset with no age given. 'He had never presented ocular manifestations' was used to exclude uveitis, cataract and glaucoma; visual impairment was left 'not reported'. 'No spleen or liver enlargement' excludes splenomegaly; the composite 'hepatomegaly or hepatic granulomas' was left 'not reported' (narrow absence). 'No cranial nerve involvement' does not exclude the composite neuropathy item. Fever is excluded from 'He denied fever ... over the previous weeks', a statement about the weeks before the myelopathy presentation. 'No inflamed joints' and 'no acute skin lesions' at the current examination are recorded as excluded feature rows but do not override the documented history of recurrent arthritis and rash in the checklist (different time points, not a contradiction). Neurological findings belong to the etanercept-induced myelopathy episode, recorded as features of the patient. 'Blood analyses were unremarkable' (apart from ESR) was not used to exclude anything more specific. No contradictions found.
